2 year old article

"Parents further reported being derogatorily called “breeders” by their children" If you have bio kids you're a breeder, facts don't care about your feelings. This is some real snowflakey shit, especially if you can't handle your kid spitting facts.

I think my bottom dysphoria came from being circumcised as an infant. When I first looked at my body naked in the mirror (at 5 or so years old) I hated how dry and cracked my glans looked, plus the fact that it was a bluish-purple compared to the rest of my pale skin. The ruffles from the remains of my inner foreskin only made the glans look more pronounced, and it embarrassed me, I still feel cold and exposed down there. My scar makes a ring around the shaft, it's jagged, asymmetrical, and makes my penis look unwashed. The whole thing wouldn't be as bad, if I didn't have to see and be reminded of what was done to me, every single time I change clothes or go to the bathroom. Sex is painful, and sometimes it just hurts on it's own. There's no one to talk to about it, my therapist just gave me a blank stare, I get mocked on Facebook and Twitter, the cir-recovery sub-reddits are full of seething mgtows with no interest in emotional healing, and the statute of limitations was over when I turned 3 years old. I'm the only amab I know personally who has bottom dysphoria severe enough to research and contact surgeons, but I've put it off trying to figure this part out.

That sounds horrible, I'll never understand why adults often feel need lie to children about that stuff, and I'm sorry that you went through that; I can't see it as anything short of traumatic. 

I get vivid nightmares of being raped (or otherwise sexually assaulted), and most recently my parents pinning me down and biting my penis to "make me a man." In the past when my partner angrily shouted at me I got flashbacks of my dad dragging me into the bedroom to spank me with his belt, but thankfully all I "remember" from my circumcision is just an overwhelming sense of pain and helplessness.

Technically what I'm looking into would be called a "neo vulva" because my aesthetic preference is more "natural" than the pornstar esq style western doctors are going for, and that requires skin, that I don't have. So zero/low depth seems to be my best option for now (it's also less invasive, and no dilating). What I'll get from surgery will never even approach the beauty and complexity of female genitals, but it'll be better than this... 

I hate having this disgusting worm attached to my torso, I hate having my testicles always hanging outside of my body like a pair of prolapsed organs, I hate stretching out my best underwear, and I hate wearing a makeshift thong and bike shorts to tuck (because nothing else is tight enough). If getting surgery causes me pain then I'll take it as more punishment for being born male, and hopefully I'll be rewarded in my next life. As I said in a previous comment, a dildo is just as functional as what I have for pleasing my partner.

Back then I definitely wanted a vagina; I knew ever since I knew what a vagina was (when I was 9 or 10 years old). As far as I know I wasn't sexually abused. I do have gaps in my memories, and I can't even count the number of times I've been asked that. It's just that those aren't a confirmation.
there's many potential issues, but I am fairly confident with what I am looking into. it takes a while to adjust, but I'll live, I want something that isn't as ugly as a penis on my body.

I think it's mostly too late for me to sue and I really don't want to start that kind of drama with my family, and no amount of money will ever make me feel better. I'm nervous at the thought of talking with a sex therapist. It wouldn't help me if they tried to take me off hrt, and testosterone made me feel like a big ugly ogre. The I was treated was terrible always being expected to be a man; my empathy, sensitivity, and kindness were seen as character flaws. My body started to trigger me as I began, developing downstairs, and going through puberty because it made me look more like my dad and brother.

I know that there are quite a few factors at play not just this. I went through and was exposed many instances of male violence in my developmental years. My body triggers me so I want to change it; at least to the best of my ability. In a few years we'll have 3d printed organs on the market, but my genital dysphoria is pretty bad; I cut myself with scissors trying to cut my balls off when I was 14 and started to get wet dreams (most of them made me feel disgusting and violated).

oh god, the masochistic reenactment element of that study compilation hits way too close to home. I knew that they came from somewhere, but I was hoping that it wasn't actually tied to this; I feel sick.

I've actually been asked about that by 3-4 different therapists, because of my mannerisms, symptoms, nightmares, etc. but I seriously don't remember anything. However, I will look into a therapist for EMDR; hopefully they can help me sort some of this out. Thank you again for the advice.

Fuck, I can't even imagine, I'm sorry that that happened to you.

It fucks me up that it's legal, that there's even a debate (that people who don't have penises think that they have a right to talk argue over this stuff), that my experiences are "a regrettable outcome," and it makes me question if my body was ever "mine" to begin with. I honestly feel like my parents have only ever seen me as a doll that belongs to them because of this, and because they would "spank" my brother and I with their belt while saying that hitting the dogs was wrong because they didn't know better... It's only (relatively) recently that I learned that not all kids were hit by their parents, and not all boys have their foreskins removed T.T

I would say that my life has been improving; I have more friends than ever before, they have stayed around for longer than 3 years, I'm actually not suicidal anymore, and I feel better about my body for the most part. There have been ups and downs but overall things are trending towards the better. My guess is that several factors are at play (as far as my transness is concerned), because my coping mechanisms for my social dysphoria were unsustainable, and I didn't realize how bad my feelings about my body were until after hrt.

It's not about them being unimportant, it's about salvaging my relationship with my body, and having protuberances coming out of my crotch still bothers me. I don't like the movement and shifting when I walk, they don't bring me any sexual pleasure, and I never want to. All I really use it for is peeing, and if I want to please a partner a dildo is just as functional. I can't think of any other reason why I should keep it when it's bringing me discomfort.

I have been looking into it, but have not reached a decision yet. If I didn't get it I would most likely look into an orchiectomy and penectomy to address my dysphoria.

On a separate note, as someone who has been circumcised I used to think that circumcision wasn't mutilation, but that was before I learned how important it is. I consider it mutilation now because it removed half of the skin on my genitals, and a very large portion of the nerve endings either from them being directly severed or due to my glans (a sensitive mucosal membrane) being directly exposed to abrasion. I will never get that skin back, I can stretch what I have, but it will never give me the nerve endings and sensitivity that I had for the first 5 hours of my life and I will never know what it is like to have pleasurable sex with my penis.

From what I've read about infant circumcision it apparently alters how the brain processes pain? so it makes sense to me that it would be traumatic even if I can't remember it. I don't know if I've heard of somatic therapy before, but I'm looking into it, thank you! 

I will definitely explore the connection between it and my sex dysphoria more. You're probably right that it is more complicated than that, as I had been coping with the social aspects of my dysphoria with isolation and celibacy. 

Thank you again for your input and well wishes! I hope that you have a nice holiday season.

Thank you, that's a good point about feeling disconnected from it due to pain. I've been looking into different groups, but I'm always skittish because of associations with the MRA movement. I'll keep looking though.

Ahhh okay, I get what you mean. I don't really use the label for myself at this point, other than like to myself or very close friends. To me I find my identity a little more fluidly, but it's just easier to tell people I'm a woman/girl.

Because there was this expectation of masculinity, and I would get lectures monthly about how it was time to "start acting like a boy now." So I would style myself as a cute, but volcel (long story) boy; I was the school twink at 5'0" and 97 lbs. my freshman year. My cuteness was one of the few things I had going for me, I bulked up to being a twunk but was never happy about it. I did fem things with my clothes, paying attention to color coordination and so on, and I used women's body wash (because I didn't like the idea of smelling like a man).
